title: CLIP-Count: Towards Text-Guided Zero-Shot Object Counting
property: object count (text-specified zero-shot counting on real images)
why_added: trained text-guided counter tested on held-out FSC-147 classes; named by T2ICount, p. 9
reads: Clean RGB photos at 224x224 through frozen CLIP ViT-B/16 with 20 visual prompts per layer; the class-name text embedding enters through cross-attention on 14x14 patch features; never reads noisy diffusion inputs
trained_on: FSC-147 training classes with class-name prompts and dot-derived density maps; 30 epochs contrastive loss, then 200 epochs MSE; per-split class counts are not printed
unseen: yes for FSC-147 validation and test classes, stated not to overlap training (test MAE 17.78); no result by count, nothing near a count of two, and no test with text naming a different class
headline: FSC-147 held-out test classes: MAE 17.78 objects per image against 22.09 for Xu et al.; no-text counters are lower (CounTR 14.71, LOCA 16.22, RCC 17.12); CLIP ViT-B/16, lower is better
copy_or_avoid: Copy the class-disjoint split; add right-word, wrong-word and no-word tests because no-text counters beat it, and do not use it as evidence for telling one subject from two (inferred)

quotes.text: We freeze both encoders in pretrained CLIP and append a small amount of learnable prompts
quotes.supports: reads: frozen CLIP with learned prompts

quotes.text: We use OpenAI pre-trained CLIP with ViTB/16 backbone
we use the deep version of VPT, with 20 visual prompts in each layer
we downsample the training images to 224×224
the MHCA propagates semantic information embedded in text to visual features
where 𝑝 = 14 denotes the number of image patches per column and row
The model is trained on the training set of FSC-147.
we use the class name as the text prompt
pre-train the model with contrastive loss only for 30 epochs before further train it with mean square error (MSE) loss for 200 epochs
our objective is to estimate a density map
quotes.supports: gradient_enters: output is a density map for counting, with no sampler
